name: English
tagline: Market data. Trade execution. One Python client.
intro: An asynchronous Python interface for Bynix, built for trading applications, data pipelines and developer tools.

capabilities.name: Free/open core
capabilities.text: MIT-licensed public package; public market data works without an account, with optional browser, network, and DataFrame extras.

capabilities.name: Fast market data
capabilities.text: Stream-first ticks, forming/closed candles, bounded historical pages, and concurrent candle batches with REST fallback.

capabilities.name: Multi-login and client pool
capabilities.text: Token, password, browser, and OTP-capable providers plus independent named clients and account events.

capabilities.name: Safe caller-owned automation
capabilities.text: ExecutionOrchestrator/AutoExecutor accepts explicit application intents with dry-run, demo-only defaults, cooldown, concurrency limits, and no uncertain-order retry.

capabilities.name: Pure indicators
capabilities.text: Decimal SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, ATR, and stochastic measurements over caller-owned data; no signals or strategy.

capabilities.name: Execution conveniences
capabilities.text: `buy_and_wait`, `sell`/early close, settlement wait, journaling, and reconciliation around explicit one-order-at-a-time calls.

capabilities.name: Verified Bynix scope
capabilities.text: Read the matrix for implemented, offline-tested, and live-demo-observed behavior; unsupported parity is not implied.

features: Session tokens, password login, browser-assisted login and 2FA callbacks.
Asset discovery, exact symbol lookup, availability and payout information.
Recent candles and paginated historical OHLCV with UTC timestamps.
Live ticks, forming/closed candles and automatic REST polling fallback.
Explicit demo, real and funded orders, settlement lookup and early close.
Durable order records, restart recovery and duplicate-reference protection.
Independent named clients, account events and detailed balances.
HTTP/SOCKS5 proxies, custom DNS and trusted-domain connection fallback.
Streaming market sentiment using the platform-style candle and tick model.
Decimal-preserving CSV/JSON export, optional pandas and candle resampling.
install_text: Install the published package from PyPI. Add optional browser, networking and DataFrame integrations as needed.
quickstart_text: Public market data works without an account. This complete example retrieves candles and reads three incoming ticks.
auth_text: Use the interactive login command, import an existing Bynix access token, or configure a password/browser provider. Login stores a local session; Python applications can also supply their own session provider. Use the client in an async context manager.
execution_text: With a connected authenticated client, place an explicit demo order and await the server result. Demo is the default account. Real or funded execution requires allow_real_trading=True; funded orders also require challenge_id. Keep order IDs and use SQLiteJournal for restart recovery.
network_text: Persistent connections, resubscription and bounded queues support continuous consumers. Auto mode uses the platform's REST tick endpoint when streaming is unavailable. Network extras enable authenticated SOCKS5 and custom DNS. Configure the same route on your authentication provider.
cli_text: Inspect the platform, stream prices, export candles and check published domains from the terminal. The CLI supplies public data directly and uses a saved session for account commands.
docs_text: Detailed signatures, return values, runnable examples and recovery behavior are documented below. Use exact trade_symbol values from the asset catalog.
validation_text: The validation record lists tested Python versions, asset/timeframe coverage, demo execution, interrupted connections and measured performance. Reproducible tests and benchmark inputs accompany the source.
paper_text: PyBynix's architecture, protocol adaptation, and dual-supervisor design are documented in the Documentation section above (see Architecture and Protocol). The full empirical evaluation, benchmark methodology, and live soak results are published as an open-access preprint on Zenodo.
contribute_text: Contributions, reproducible bug reports and documentation improvements are welcome. PyBynix is independently maintained; platform and language trademarks remain with their owners.
whats_new: **Market session.** Market data is no longer anonymous: the client obtains and refreshes a market session automatically, and falls back to a guest session when no account is configured.
**Sealed payloads.** Market responses now arrive encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305 and are opened transparently; a pure-Python RFC 8439 path means no compiled dependency is required.
**Encrypted streams.** Socket subscriptions carry the market session id, and ticks are opened with a rotating keyring that the client refreshes across each rotation.
**One session per account.** A market session can be shared between a REST client and its socket shards via `Bynix(market_session=...)`, which the platform requires.
**Platform limits.** `client.market_limits` exposes the allowance the platform reports: history calls per minute, maximum candles per request and subscriptions.
**Clearer failures.** A Cloudflare challenge on a market call raises `ChallengeRequired` instead of a bare `403`, so an IP block is distinguishable from an authentication problem.
